quotelist.quote: Handbuilt in the USA - Every Lib Tech board is handmade by snowboarders with jobs in the USA.
1 Year Warranty - Covered under manufacturer warranty for 1 year from the time of purchase.
Warranty includes structural defects only and DOES NOT cover impact damage, abuse, misuse or normal wear and tear.
Birch Internal Sidewalls - Rugged, lightweight, vertical end grain Birch internal sidewalls add pop and durability.
UHMW Sintered Sidewalls - A Lib Tech innovation that is twice as sintered as most industry sidewalls.

citation.reasoning: Tactics is a well-established specialty board retailer. These are factual product specs and warranty details directly pulled from the product page, matching manufacturer claims.

quotelist.quote: ALL MOUNTAIN - DIRECTIONAL TWIN
The DPR is a developmental project realized. Lib Co-founder Pete Saari and crew spent 10 years developing the Double Dip to freestyle perfection.
The DPR is focused on making the most of your local resort terrain every day with an eye on agile trenched carving, trick progression, switch landings and ripping pow days when they come your way.
The early rise nose is forgiving, initiates turns effortlessly and floats pow.
A mild camber brings the board to life and adds powerful pop in the tail.
A radial sidecut with mini-mag and equal nose and tail widths make this a very user friendly freestyle stick in the park or blasting side hits.

citation.reasoning: Official Lib Tech manufacturer product page — the most authoritative source for specs, sizing, and product description. The spec table extracted contains complete sizing data for all lengths. Price listed as $499.99. Note: this page currently shows the 25/26 model year but the board design/specs carry forward to 2027.

quotelist.quote: This directional twin features an Early Rise Camber profile for powerful pop and effortless turns, combined with the unmatched edge hold of Magne-Traction®.
Built with a lightweight OP core and a fast TNT base, the DPR delivers a responsive and smooth ride in any condition.
Mid Flex (around 6/10): Offers a versatile balance of responsiveness for carving and forgiveness for playful riding.

citation.reasoning: Salty Peaks is a specialty snowboard retailer selling the 2027 model. Their product descriptions confirm key specs including flex, camber type, and construction details.

quotelist.quote: For this season I had the opportunity to put the new 2026 Lib Tech dPr Snowboard through the wringer.
This board is the epitome of an all-mountain machine with a freestyle twist.
The dPr handled everything I threw at it—groomers, hardpack, powder, spring slush—and always left me wanting more.

citation.reasoning: evo is one of the most reputable specialty outdoor retailers. This is a field-tested review from a season-long tester — highly credible for rider experience claims.

quotelist.quote: The Lib Tech dPr has earned an 88.15 out of a possible 100 score (or 4.41 out 5) stars.
You get a lot of snowboard tech in the dPr for the low price of $499.99.
With how smooth this board rides, it feels closer to compare this to a snowboard that is in the $650 to $700 price range.
The Lib Tech DPR costs $31.98 more than the average snowboard price of $468.01.
Ranks 11th out of the 38 boards reviewed in the all mountain category.
Ranks 11th out of the 36 boards reviewed in the park category.
The base on this board is decently fast, and since it's all black, it is so easy to repair with a black P-Tex stick.
It'll just look like a black Lib Tech board with a smiley face on its base.
The Magne Traction built into this board makes the Lib Tech dPr an excellent option for East Coast riders or anyone who needs extra grip in icy conditions.
The dPr is available in 152cm, 154cm, 156cm, 158cm, 159W, and 160cm sizes.

citation.reasoning: Board of the World is a dedicated snowboard review site with a consistent scoring methodology. The reviewer (Steve Weber) rode the 156cm at Stratton VT on icy conditions, which provides particularly relevant data for ice performance. Affiliate-funded site but uses consistent metrics.

quotelist.quote: The board is handcrafted in the Mervin factory in the USA, with attention to quality and sustainability.
Mervin Manufacturing, founded in 1977 by Mike Olson and Pete Saari, is the leading manufacturer of Lib Tech snowboards.
With a focus on environmental friendliness and local production, the company is based in Sequim, Washington, and remains the last major board factory in the US.

citation.reasoning: European snowboard information site providing contextual details about the manufacturer. Claims are consistent with official Mervin Manufacturing sources.

quotelist.quote: Lib Tech co-founder Pete Saari and crew spent over a decade refining the Double Dip, and the DPR takes those lessons in sidecut, geometry, and balance and applies them to a modern freestyle platform.
Original Power Construction (OP) – Lightweight, durable build tuned for daily resort freestyle riding.
Core: 75% Aspen / 25% Paulownia – Poppy, responsive core with reduced weight.
Directional Twin Freestyle Shape – Balanced nose and tail widths with a directional outline for confident switch riding and added drive when riding forward.
